stories.title: Equinix accelerates AI inference for enterprises with NVIDIA and Together AI
stories.summary: Equinix is broadening its long-running partnership with NVIDIA to launch Equinix Inference Exchange, a distributed AI inference program that also involves Together AI. The initiative is aimed at delivering inference capabilities to enterprise customers across Equinix's global footprint.
stories.why_it_matters: Colocation providers are racing to capture inference workloads, which require low-latency capacity close to end users rather than the massive centralized campuses used for training. Equinix's move positions its interconnection-rich metros, including those across APAC, as enterprise AI delivery points and sharpens competition with cloud on-ramps and edge providers.
stories.content:
Global digital infrastructure firm Equinix has announced that it is expanding its longtime collaboration with NVIDIA to deliver Equinix® Inference Exchange, a distributed AI inference program for global enterprises, alongside a new collaboration with Together AI.

In a press release, Equinix explained that as enterprise AI moves from experimentation to production, inference increasingly needs to run closer to the users, data and applications it serves across clouds, models, providers and geographies. Equinix Inference Exchange aims to offer enterprises a faster path from AI experimentation to production, with secure, low-latency connectivity to the data, users and ecosystem they depend on.

![](https://w.media/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/New-Sponsor-Banner.jpg)

This collaboration brings together Equinix, NVIDIA and TogetherAI. Equinix provides the infrastructure foundation, including power, advanced cooling and day-two operations, connected through Equinix Fabric to the clouds, networks and AI providers that inference depends on. Meanwhile, NVIDIA anchors the build with its Enterprise Reference Architectures and AI infrastructure purpose-built to maximize AI factory throughput and minimize token cost. Finally, Together AI runs the platform on top, supporting both multi-tenant deployments for shared efficiency and dedicated single-tenant environments for workloads that require dedicated capacity.

Adaire Fox-Martin, CEO, Equinix said, “Our longtime relationship with NVIDIA delivers the accelerated computing foundation at the heart of modern AI, while Together AI’s commitment to open ecosystems gives enterprises the flexibility to scale on their terms. Equinix Inference Exchange will enable architectures that are neutral by design, open by default and engineered for exceptional performance.”

Raj Mirpuri, Vice President, Global AI clouds and infrastructure ecosystem, NVIDIA said, “As accelerated compute becomes a strategic asset class, combining NVIDIA’s infrastructure & technology with Together AI’s open-model inference platform and Equinix’s global reach gives enterprises a powerful, distributed foundation to bring intelligence closer to their data, applications and customers—accelerating the next generation of intelligent services.”

![](https://w.media/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/Issue-13-Banner-1.jpg)

“Together AI was built on the conviction that open, accessible AI is what will define the industry moving forward, because enterprises shouldn’t have to choose between model performance and operational flexibility,” said Vipul Ved Prakash, co-founder and CEO, Together AI. “What we are building with Equinix and NVIDIA proves that model choice and performance are not trade-offs. They are the foundation of enterprise AI done right.”

Built on Equinix Fabric, the solution will connect to inference providers across major metros worldwide, cutting time-to-first-token. It also will connect to an expansive ecosystem of clouds, networks and AI providers, reducing deployment complexity. Equinix Inference Exchange will be available starting in Q1 2027.

stories.title: Equinix launches managed AI cloud connectivity service
stories.summary: Equinix has introduced Equinix Fabric One, a managed connectivity service for links spanning AI, cloud, and enterprise environments. The offering is built on open connectivity specifications developed by AWS and other industry players.
stories.why_it_matters: Adopting open specifications rather than a proprietary stack lowers switching friction for enterprises and could standardize how AI infrastructure interconnects across providers. The launch intensifies competition in the cloud on-ramp and interconnection market that underpins hybrid AI deployments across APAC metros.
stories.content:
![Equinix launches managed AI cloud connectivity service](https://datacenternews.asia/uploads/story/2026/09/03/chris-audie_chief-product-officer-story-318142.webp) 

# Equinix launches managed AI cloud connectivity service

Thu, 3rd Sep 2026 (Today)
![Joseph Gabriel Lagonsin](https://datacenternews.asia/rails/active_storage/representations/redirect/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsiZGF0YSI6MTYyNSwicHVyIjoiYmxvYl9pZCJ9fQ==--675a9c66bfe11204f24f3bdaad09013f83135297/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsiZGF0YSI6eyJmb3JtYXQiOiJ3ZWJwIiwicmVzaXplX3RvX2ZpbGwiOlsxNjAsMTYwXSwicXVhbGl0eSI6ODV9LCJwdXIiOiJ2YXJpYXRpb24ifX0=--89ddf5e6765c65a563c2258053e9d33c05d195da/Joseph%20Headshot.webp) 

Equinix has launched Equinix Fabric One, a managed connectivity service for links across AI, cloud and enterprise environments. The service uses open connectivity specifications developed by AWS and Google Cloud.

The product is designed to reduce the manual work involved in building and managing network links between multiple providers, sites and workloads. Customers specify what they want connected, while Equinix manages the underlying routing, cloud links, encryption, resiliency and failover as a single service.

The launch comes as companies face growing complexity in connecting distributed infrastructure for multicloud and AI workloads. Equinix is positioning the service as a way to abstract that complexity, shifting network setup from a component-by-component process to a managed model based on customer intent.

Access will be available through a portal, application programming interfaces, automation workflows, agent-based requests and natural-language prompts. The underlying framework draws on the OpenAPI 3.0 Interconnect specification, an open source standard developed with input from AWS and Google Cloud.

Chris Audie, Chief Product Officer at Equinix, said the traditional model of building enterprise networks one connection at a time no longer fits distributed AI systems.

"For decades, enterprise networks have been built one connection at a time for each partner and provider they depend on. That approach doesn't scale in a world of distributed AI that demands dynamic, flexible and real-time connectivity," said Chris Audie, Chief Product Officer at Equinix.

"Equinix Fabric One will reduce the complexity that's slowing enterprises down by automatically managing connectivity across distributed architectures, based on the customer's intent," Audie said.

### Growing complexity

For many organisations, adding connections to clouds, AI providers, partners and branch locations has become a specialist task spanning networking, infrastructure and operations teams. That can delay deployment and make it harder to adapt infrastructure as business requirements change.

Andrew Buss, Senior Research Director, Cloud and Datacenters, Enterprise Infrastructure at IDC, said network operations remain reliant on manual design and provisioning.

"Networking is still a key area of enterprise infrastructure that remains heavily dependent on manual design and operations," said Andrew Buss, Senior Research Director, Cloud and Datacenters, Enterprise Infrastructure at IDC.

"Organisations are increasingly looking for ways to simplify and automate how connectivity is provisioned and managed across distributed cloud and AI environments, but achieving this transformation remains a major challenge. Advances that enable more integrated automation and intent-driven approaches can reduce operational complexity and risk while supporting the flexibility modern AI and multicloud architectures require," Buss said.

The service is built on Equinix's existing interconnection base, which includes more than 10,500 interconnected businesses and about 3,000 cloud and IT providers. Equinix also said eight of the top 10 AI model providers and nine of the top 10 neoclouds already have active deployments on its platform.

The use of an open specification is central to the product's design. Equinix said interoperability across multiple cloud and AI environments should help customers avoid being tied to a single provider while keeping architecture choices open as requirements change.

AWS and Google Cloud, which Equinix named as lead integration partners, linked their support to the open interconnect standard.

"Customers shouldn't have to figure out how to connect across multiple clouds and AI environments on their own," said Robert Kennedy, Vice President of AWS Network Services.

"They should just define what they need and have it work. Fabric One builds on the open interconnect specification that AWS and Google Cloud helped define and delivers exactly that: a managed service that handles the complexity so customers can focus on their AI workloads, not how everything connects," Kennedy said.

Google Cloud made a similar case for simpler links between platforms as AI systems spread across different environments.

"Cross-cloud interoperability is the backbone of the AI era," said Rob Enns, Vice President of Engineering, Cloud Networking, Google Cloud.

"We helped establish the open interconnect specification so enterprises no longer have to manage the complexity of multi-cloud networking. By combining Google Cloud's Cross-Cloud Network capabilities with Equinix Fabric One, we are giving customers an automated, intent-driven network that lets them quickly deploy distributed AI workloads," Enns said.

### Customer interest

Equinix also pointed to customer demand for connectivity models that reduce the burden of configuring and maintaining individual network links. That reflects a broader shift in infrastructure consumption toward managed services and automated operations.

"As technology environments become more distributed, AI workloads and multicloud architectures require connectivity that is flexible, scalable and easier to manage," said Paul Hager, CEO of Hyundai AutoEver America.

"Equinix Fabric One has the potential to accelerate our efforts to meet those needs," Hager said.

Equinix said Fabric One is expected to enter beta later this year, with general availability planned for 2027 and an initial rollout in North America.

Global investment in artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure is projected to reach US$31.6 trillion by 2050, according to PwC's Global Data Center Outlook. This growth is expected to significantly increase annual data center capital expenditure, with Asia Pacific, led by China and India, accounting for a substantial portion of this cumulative investment.

Highlights

Global AI infrastructure investment could reach US$31.6 trillion by 2050, as per PwC projections.

Annual data center capital expenditure is forecast to rise from US$800 billion (2026) to US$1.8 trillion (2050).

Asia Pacific, led by China and India, is expected to account for US$8.2 trillion in cumulative capital expenditure.

ICT equipment will constitute 93% of AI infrastructure investment by 2050, up from 70% today.

Power, connectivity, security, policy certainty, and community consent will guide global investment flows.

Global investment in artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure is projected to reach US$31.6 trillion by 2050, according to baseline figures from PwC's Global Data Center Outlook. The United States is forecast to capture nearly half, or 48 percent, of this investment, amounting to US$15.1 trillion.The report, which commissioned Oxford Economics to model data center capital expenditure across 46 countries and five regions, indicates that annual data center capital expenditure could rise from approximately US$800 billion in 2026 to US$1.8 trillion by 2050. Asia Pacific is expected to contribute US$8.2 trillion in cumulative capital expenditure, driven primarily by China and India, while sovereign AI strategies are accelerating investment in Europe and the Middle East.

Investment Drivers and ICT Dominance

PwC highlights that unlike traditional infrastructure booms, which often taper off, AI infrastructure investment is anticipated to accelerate due to the cyclical need for upgrades in chips and other Information and Communication Technology (ICT) equipment every few years. ICT equipment's share of total investment is projected to increase from 70 percent today to 93 percent by 2050.Clara Cutajar, Global Infrastructure Leader at PwC Australia, stated that AI infrastructure is becoming a defining capital allocation challenge, impacting technology, energy, real estate, supply chains, regulation, and financing. She emphasised that investors need to recognise data centers as hybrid assets with complex risk profiles, and that capturing this investment requires active positioning rather than a passive approach.

Key Factors for Investment Flow

The Outlook identifies five critical factors that will direct global investment flows: power availability, robust connectivity, stringent security measures, policy certainty, and community consent. Additionally, access to Graphics Processing Units (GPUs) is also expected to significantly influence where this investment ultimately lands.
